I'll reason through this as the farmer, then give my plan.

---

**My thinking, in my own words**

Alright, 70 mu is what I've got, and with just the three of us at home I can't do everything myself — my wife handles most of the vegetables with me, and for cotton picking and melon harvest I bring in day-labor women from the village. Six years I've been back on the land now, long enough to have my routine but I'm still not one of the old hands who can tell you everything just by looking at the sky.

Here's how I split the ground. The main 50 mu stays in wheat-maize, double-cropped like most families around here — that's my grain base and the subsidy keeps me honest on it. Out on the sandier west field I do 10 mu of cotton; it's more work but still pays better per mu than grain. Then I have one 5-mu plot that does watermelon in spring and flips to cauliflower in fall — same ground, two cash crops. And another 5 mu of chili that runs through the summer. The cash crops are where the real money is, but I don't dare put more ground into vegetables than my wife and I can manage without drowning in hired labor costs.

**Wheat (50 mu):** Plant October 8-12 right after maize comes off. I use Jimai — the agri-station pushed it a few years back and it's held up. Buy fresh seed every two or three years, save my own in between. Before planting I broadcast about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15) per mu, then at jointing in March I topdress 20 kg of urea. That's around 15 kg of nitrogen total — the extension fellow said I could go lighter but my neighbor Lao Wang tried cutting back and his yield tanked, so I'm not chasing that. Three irrigations: winter water, green-up, grain-fill. I expect 450-480 kg/mu if spring rain is decent.

**Maize (50 mu):** Straight after wheat in mid-June, six-day window at most. I use a no-till planter that drops seed and fertilizer together — rent it from the co-op. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu depending on what the shop has. Base is about 35 kg of 18-9-9 compound, then at big-trumpet stage I top with 15 kg of urea. Rain usually covers the water but July gets dry so I'll irrigate once or twice. Target around 500 kg/mu.

**Cotton (10 mu):** Film-mulched, planted mid-April, hybrid seed. Base 30 kg compound, side-dress another 25 kg of urea when budding starts. Needs spraying — at least twice for bollworm and aphids. Picking starts September and runs into October, three or four rounds. I hire four or five village women for picking — that's my biggest cash outlay on cotton. Lint maybe 250 kg/mu.

**Watermelon (5 mu):** "8424" type, planted end of April under small arches. Drip line from the well, heavy fertilizer — I don't cut corners on melons, the price swing is too big to gamble on a small crop. Harvest mid-July and the Handan buyer comes to the village.

**Cauliflower (5 mu):** Same ground as the melons. Transplant early August right after pulling vines — I have to clean up and rotary-till fast. Sell to the same buyer in November. Watch for aphids and caterpillars, spray two or three times.

**Chili (5 mu):** Transplant early May with drip. Pick multiple times July through September, dry the last ones for storage. Constant work but steady money.

I keep a cash reserve. The pump breaking or a bad price year can ruin you if you've spent everything on inputs.
